copy.en:
Do stars live forever?

Nope! Stars have a life cycle—they are born, shine for millions of years, and finally die.
copy.tl:
Magpakailanman ba ang mga bituin?

Hindi! May buhay ang mga bituin—isinisilang sila, nagniningning ng milyon-milyong taon, at sa wakas ay namamatay.
copy.bis:
Magpakailanman ba ang mga bituon?

Dili! Ang mga bituon may kinabuhi—natawo sila, mosidlak sulod sa milyon-milyong tuig, ug sa kataposan mamatay.

copy.en: Bigger stars burn fuel faster! A star 10 times the Sun's mass lives 10 million years, our Sun lives 10 billion, and a small red dwarf lives over a trillion years.
copy.tl: Mas mabilis masunog ang fuel ng mas mabibigat na bituin! Ang 10 beses mas mabigat sa Araw mabuhay ng 10 milyong taon, ang Araw ng 10 bilyon, at red dwarf ng higit isang trilyon.

copy.en:
Where does a star spend most of its life?

In the main sequence! Here, it burns hydrogen through nuclear fusion in its core. Our Sun is currently midway through this phase.
copy.tl:
Saan ginugugol ng bituin ang karamihan ng buhay nito?

Sa main sequence! Dito, nagsusunog ito ng hydrogen sa pamamagitan ng nuclear fusion sa core nito. Ang Araw natin ay nasa gitna na ng phase na ito.
copy.bis:
Asa gigugol sa bituin ang kadaghanan sa iyang kinabuhi?

Sa main sequence! Dinhi, nagsunog kini og hydrogen pinaagi sa nuclear fusion sa iyang core. Ang atong Adlaw naa sa katagatnga niining phase.

copy.en: In about 5 billion years, our Sun will expand into a red giant that might swallow the inner planets! Later, it will leave behind a planetary nebula and a small, hot white dwarf.
copy.tl: Humigit-kumulang 5 bilyong taon na, ang Araw natin ay magiging red giant na baka lamonin ang mga panloob na planeta! Kalaunan, mag-iiwan ito ng planetary nebula at isang maliit, mainit na white dwarf.
copy.bis: Mga 5 bilyong tuig na karon, ang atong Adlaw molapad ngadto sa red giant nga basin molunok sa mga panloob nga planeta! Unya, mobiya kini og planetary nebula ug usa ka gamay, init nga white dwarf.

copy.en: A bright star isn't always huge! It might just be close to us. Giant, powerful stars can look dim if they are extremely far away.
copy.tl: Hindi laging malaki ang maliwanag na bituin! Baka malapit lang ito sa atin. Ang mga napakalaking bituin ay mukhang madilim kung sobrang layo.
copy.bis: Dili gyud dagko ang tanan hayag nga bituon! Basin duol ra kini kanato. Ang tinuod nga dagkong bituon murag hanap kung hilabihan kalayo.

copy.en:
Can a star's color tell us how hot it is?

Yes! Blue stars are the hottest, red and orange are cooler, and our yellow Sun is right in the middle!
copy.tl:
Maaari bang malaman sa kulay ng bituin kung gaano ito kainit?

Oo! Ang asul ang pinakamainit, ang pula at orange ay mas malamig, at ang dilaw na Araw natin ay nasa gitna!
copy.bis:
Mahibaw-an ba sa kolor sa bituon kung unsa kainit kini?

Oo! Ang asul ang labing init, ang pula ug orange mas bugnaw, ug ang dalag nga Adlaw naa ra sa tunga!

copy.en:
Think there are only a few stars in the sky?

We see only a few thousand, but there are billions of stars in the universe! City lights hide even more.
copy.tl:
Akala mo ba konti lang ang mga bituin sa kalangitan?

Ilan sa libo lang ang nakikita natin, pero may bilyon-bilyong bituin sa uniberso! Sa lungsod, mas konti pa dahil sa ilaw.
copy.bis:
Sa akala ba nimo gamay ra ang mga bituon sa langit?

Pipila ka libo ra ang makita nato, apan adunay binilyon ka bituon sa uniberso! Sa siyudad, mas gamay pa tungod sa kahayag.

copy.en: A star shines because of nuclear fusion! It joins hydrogen to make helium and releases energy.
copy.tl: Nagniningning ang bituin dahil sa nuclear fusion! Pinagsasama nito ang hydrogen para gumawa ng helium at maglabas ng enerhiya.
copy.bis: Nagsiga ang bituon tungod sa nuclear fusion! Gihiusa niini ang hydrogen aron mahimong helium ug mogawas ang enerhiya.

copy.en: Stars don't shine forever! They eventually run out of hydrogen fuel and begin to change. Some last billions of years, seeming endless, but they all have an end.
copy.tl: Hindi magpakailanman nagliliwanag ang mga bituin! Sa kalaunan, mauubos ang hydrogen fuel nila at magbabago. Ang ilan ay tatagal ng bilyong taon, pero may katapusan din sila.
copy.bis: Dili magpakailanman magsiga ang mga bituon! Sa kadugayan, mahurot ang ilang hydrogen fuel ug magbag-o sila. Ang uban molungtad og binilyon ka tuig, apan adunay gihapon kataposan.

copy.en:
Are we looking into the past when we see stars?

Yes! Starlight takes years to reach Earth. The light we see tonight actually left those faraway stars many years ago!
copy.tl:
Nakikita ba natin ang nakaraan kapag tumitingin tayo sa mga bituin?

Oo! Napakatagal ng byahe ng liwanag ng bituin. Ang nakikita natin ngayon ay umalis na sa kanila maraming taon na ang nakalipas!
copy.bis:
Nagtan-aw ba ta sa nangagi kung motan-aw ta sa mga bituon?

Oo! Dugay kaayo mobiyahe ang kahayag sa bituon. Ang makita nato karon mibiya na kini daghang tuig na ang milabay!

copy.en:
Does a star burn like fire?

Nope! Fire needs oxygen and wood, but space has none. A star's light actually comes from fusion, not burning!
copy.tl:
Nasusunog ba ang bituin tulad ng apoy?

Hindi! Kailangan ng apoy ang oxygen at kahoy, pero wala nito sa kalawakan. Ang liwanag ng bituin ay galing sa fusion, hindi sa pagkasunog!
copy.bis:
Nagdilaab ba ang bituon sama sa kalayo?

Dili! Ang kalayo nanginahanglan og oxygen ug kahoy, apan wala niana sa kawanangan. Ang kahayag sa bituon gikan sa fusion, dili sa pagkasunog!

copy.en: Stars twinkle because their light bends through our moving atmosphere! The shifting air makes the light shiver, but the star itself isn't flickering.
copy.tl: Kumikislap ang mga bituin dahil yumuyuko ang liwanag sa gumagalaw na hangin ng atmospera! Nanginginig ang liwanag, pero hindi talaga kumikislap ang bituin.
copy.bis: Nagkidlap ang mga bituon tungod kay moliko ang kahayag sa naglihok nga hangin sa atmospera! Nagkurog ang kahayag, pero dili gyud magkidlap ang bituon.

copy.en:
Ever wonder how to tell a star from a planet?

Stars make their own light from fusion! Planets don't. They only shine by reflecting sunlight.
copy.tl:
Napapagkamalan mo ba ang planeta sa bituin?

Ang bituin ay gumagawa ng sariling liwanag mula sa fusion! Ang planeta naman, sinasalamin lang nito ang liwanag ng Araw.
copy.bis:
Naglibog ba kon unsay lahi sa bituon ug planeta?

Ang bituon naghimo og kaugalingong kahayag gikan sa fusion! Ang planeta, gipakita lang niini ang kahayag sa Adlaw.

copy.en:
How do massive stars create heavy elements like gold and silver?

They end their lives in a powerful explosion called a supernova! This creates heavy elements like iron, gold, and silver, scattering them into space for new stars and planets.
copy.tl:
Paano gumawa ng ginto at pilak ang malalaking bituin?

Tinatapos nila ang buhay sa makapangyarihang supernova! Lumilikha ito ng mabibigat na elemento tulad ng bakal, ginto, at pilak, na kakalat sa kalawakan para sa bagong bituin at planeta.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo og bulawan ug plata sa dagkong bituin?

Gitapos nila ang kinabuhi sa gamhanan nga supernova! Nagmugna kini og mabug-at nga elemento sama sa puthaw, bulawan, ug plata, ug nagkuyanap niini sa kalawakan para sa bag-ong bituin ug planeta.

copy.en:
How do astronomers measure huge distances in space?

They use Cepheid variable stars! These stars pulse in a predictable pattern. By studying their brightness cycle, astronomers use them as 'standard candles' to measure universe distances!
copy.tl:
Paano sinusukat ng mga astronomer ang malalayong distansya sa space?

Gumagamit sila ng Cepheid variable stars! Nagpapaliwanag ang mga bituin na ito sa predictable pattern. Ginagamit ng mga astronomer ang brightness cycle nila bilang 'standard candle' para sukatin ang distansya!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsukod sa mga astronomer sa layo nga distansya sa space?

Naggamit sila og Cepheid variable stars! Kining mga bituin nagpulso sa predictable pattern. Gigamit sa mga astronomer ang ilang brightness cycle isip 'standard candle' aron sukdon ang distansya sa universe!

copy.en: Did you know there's a fourth state of matter? It's called plasma, and you can find it in the sun and in lightning!
copy.tl: Alam mo ba na may ikaapat na anyo ng bagay? Ito ay plasma, at makikita ito sa araw at sa kidlat!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga naay ikaupat nga kahimtang sa butang? Kini mao ang plasma, ug makita kini sa adlaw ug sa kilat!

copy.en: Matter can change between three states—solid, liquid, and gas—when heat is added or removed.
copy.tl: Ang matter ay maaaring magbago sa tatlong estado—solid, liquid, at gas—kapag dinagdagan o binawasan ng init.
copy.bis: Ang matter mahimong mausab sa tulo ka estado—solid, liquid, ug gas—kon dugangan o kuhaan og init.

It only shares background context related to the topic.

copy.en: Long ago, ancient people rubbed amber—a hard yellow tree resin—and it pulled tiny leaves and feathers! The Greek word for amber, 'elektron,' gave us the word electricity!
copy.tl: Noong unang panahon, kinuskos ng mga sinaunang tao ang amber—isang matigas na dilaw na dagta ng puno—at hinihila nito ang maliliit na dahon at balahibo! Mula sa Griyegong 'elektron,' nanggaling ang salitang electricity!
copy.bis: Kaniadto, gikuskos sa karaang mga tawo ang amber—gahi nga dalag nga resin sa kahoy—ug gibira niini ang gagmay nga dahon ug balhibo! Gikan sa Griyego nga 'elektron,' naggikan ang pulong electricity!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They get opposite charges and attract each other
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why dried clothes cling due to static electricity, but it does not involve investigating the effects using the specified common materials (comb, plastic/glass rods, balloons) nor any guided investigation. It only provides a conceptual explanation of a static electricity effect, so it does not directly support the competency's investigative activity.

copy.en:
Why do clothes cling together after drying?

As clothes tumble and rub, electrons move between them. They get opposite charges and attract each other, making them stick together like magic!
copy.tl:
Bakit nagkakadikit ang damit pagkatuyo?

Habang naghahaluan at nagkukuskosan ang damit, naglilipat ang electron. Nagkakaroon sila ng magkapalitang charge at nag-a-attract, kaya nagdidikit sila!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga nagdikit ang mga sinina human mauga?

Samtang nag-uros ug nagkuskos ang sinina, mobalhin ang electron. Naay magbalhiay nga charge ug magdani, mao nga magdikit sila!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rubbing makes tiny electrons jump from one object to another!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the mechanism of static charge (electron transfer) but does not involve investigating effects using common materials like a comb, plastic/glass rods, or balloons. It provides conceptual background rather than supporting the investigation skill.

copy.en:
How does rubbing things together create static force?

Rubbing makes tiny electrons jump from one object to another! The loser becomes positive, the winner becomes negative. These opposite charges attract each other!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Steel is super strong without being too thick or heavy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses steel, a metal, and its strength and use in bridges, but the competency specifically targets metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper. Steel is not one of the named examples, and the card does not identify properties/uses of those specific metals. It only shares a general property of steel, so it is related but not direct support.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Steel is super strong without being too thick or heavy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes steel as strong and light, which are physical properties, but the competency asks to describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card does not describe these general properties or provide a broader lesson on solid materials; it focuses on steel's comparative strength and weight in a specific context. This is related vocabulary but not direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Why do tall buildings and large bridges use steel?

Steel is super strong without being too thick or heavy! If we used pure iron or stone, they'd need to be huge to stand. Steel makes strong, lighter beams possible.
copy.tl:
Bakit gumagamit ng steel ang mga tulay at gusali?

Sobrang lakas ng steel kahit hindi masyadong makapal o mabigat! Kung purong bakal o bato, kailangan silang sobrang bagal para tumindig. Ang steel ang nagbibigay ng malakas at magagaan na haligi.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga naggamit ug steel ang mga tulay ug building?

Lig-on kaayo ang steel bisan dili sobra kabaga o kabug-at! Kung puro puthaw o bato, kinahanglan sila sobra kabaga aron makatindog. Ang steel maoy naghatag ug lig-on ug mas gaan nga biga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Steel isn't just iron mixed with carbon! Special steels add metals like chromium, nickel, or manganese
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses alloying metals in steel (chromium, nickel, manganese) and their roles, but does not identify the properties and uses of the local community metals named in the competency (iron, gold, silver, copper). It only tangentially mentions iron as a base material, without describing its properties or uses. The content is about advanced alloying, not the grade-3 competency.

copy.en: Steel isn't just iron mixed with carbon! Special steels add metals like chromium, nickel, or manganese for superpowers—like fighting rust or extra toughness. Each metal has its own job!
copy.tl: Hindi lang carbon ang hinahalo sa bakal para sa steel! May espesyal na steel na dinadagdagan ng chromium, nickel, o manganese para sa superpowers—tulad ng laban-kalawang o dagdag tibay. Bawat metal may sariling trabaho!
copy.bis: Dili lang carbon ang isagol sa puthaw para sa steel! Adunay espesyal nga steel nga gidugangan ug chromium, nickel, o manganese para sa superpowers—sama sa batok taya o dugang kusog. Ang matag metal adunay kaugalingong trabaho!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Old scrap metal is melted and turned into new steel without losing strength.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions recycling of steel, which is a disposal/reuse concept, but it does not demonstrate proper handling or disposal of materials according to their properties, nor does it address the competency's examples (reusing objects, disposing of excess oil, recycling paper/plastic/glass). It only states that steel can be recycled by melting, providing no instructional support for the skill of proper handling/disposal.

copy.en:
What happens to old, broken steel like cars or cans?

They get recycled! Old scrap metal is melted and turned into new steel without losing strength. It's a great way to help the environment!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa mga lumang sirang steel tulad ng sasakyan o lata?

Nire-recycle sila! Ang lumang scrap metal ay tinutunaw at ginagawang bagong steel nang hindi nawawala ang lakas nito. Magandang paraan ito para tulungan ang kalikasan!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa daang guba nga steel sama sa sakyanan o lata?

Gi-recycle sila! Ang daang scrap metal tunawon ug himoong bag-ong steel nga dili mawala ang kalig-on niini. Maayo kini nga paagi aron tabangan ang kalikasan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Leaves and flowers grow attached to a plant's stem.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a basic fact about stems holding leaves and flowers, but does not address the role of plant parts in getting water and nutrients from the soil, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Leaves and flowers grow attached to a plant's stem.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The stem is part of the shoot system, but the card only notes attachment of leaves and flowers; it does not describe the root and shoot systems or explain why they are important.

copy.en: Leaves and flowers grow attached to a plant's stem.
copy.tl: Ang mga dahon at bulaklak ay nakakabit sa tangkay ng halaman.
copy.bis: Ang mga dahon ug bulak nagtubo nga nakakabit sa punoan sa tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A plant's stem lifts its leaves up high so they can reach the sunlight.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant part (stem) and its role, but the role described is reaching sunlight, not getting water and nutrients from the soil as required by the competency. It shares vocabulary about plant parts but does not directly support the competency's specific function.

copy.en: A plant's stem lifts its leaves up high so they can reach the sunlight.
copy.tl: Itinataas ng tangkay ang mga dahon para maabot nila ang sikat ng araw.
copy.bis: Ipataas sa punoan ang mga dahon aron maabot nila ang kahayag sa adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A node on a stem is where a leaf or branch grows; the space between two nodes is called an internode.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines stem nodes and internodes but does not address the role of leaves, roots, or stems in getting water and nutrients from the soil, which is the focus of G3-L-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A node on a stem is where a leaf or branch grows; the space between two nodes is called an internode.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a structural detail of the shoot system but does not explain why the root and shoot system are important, nor does it connect nodes/internodes to the function of the shoot system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A node on a stem is where a leaf or branch grows; the space between two nodes is called an internode.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a stem part but does not describe how leaf, stem, and roots work together as a transport system, which is the core of G8-L-3.

copy.en:
What is a node on a plant stem?

A node on a stem is where a leaf or branch grows; the space between two nodes is called an internode.
copy.tl:
Ano ang node sa tangkay ng halaman?

Ang node ng tangkay ay ang bahaging pinagmumulan ng dahon o sanga; ang espasyo sa pagitan ng dalawang node ay tinatawag na internode.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang node sa tangkay sa tanom?

Ang node sa tangkay mao ang bahin diin motubo ang dahon o sanga; ang espasyo tali sa duha ka node gitawag og internode.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: sheds its skin to grow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions growth (shedding skin to grow) but does not teach the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It is a specific behavioral fact about a stick insect, not a description of the characteristic of growth as a general living thing trait.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: no clue is left behind for enemies to find
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an adaptation (eating shed skin to avoid leaving clues for enemies), which is related to adaptation, but the competency specifically requires using secondary sources to describe examples of animals changing to suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. The card does not present this as an example of evolutionary change or use secondary sources; it is a simple behavioral explanation.

copy.en:
Why does a stick insect eat its own skin?

When a stick insect sheds its skin to grow, it usually eats the old skin, so no nutrients go to waste and no clue is left behind for enemies to find.
copy.tl:
Bakit kinakain ng stick insect ang sarili nitong balat?

Kapag nagpapalit ng balat ang stick insect para lumaki, karaniwan nitong kinakain ang lumang balat, para walang nasasayang na sustansya at walang bakas na maiiwan para sa mga kaaway.
copy.bis:
Nganong kaonon sa stick insect ang kaugalingon niining panit?

Kon mag-ilis og panit ang stick insect aron modako, kasagaran kaonon niini ang daan nga panit, aron walay masayang nga sustansya ug walay timailhan nga mabilin alang sa mga kaaway.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most stick insects come out and feed at night, when it's safer for them to avoid predators
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not an example of mimicry or camouflage as animals changed to better suit their environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: when it's safer for them to avoid predators
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en: Most stick insects come out and feed at night, when it's safer for them to avoid predators.
copy.tl: Karamihan sa mga stick insect ay lumalabas at kumakain tuwing gabi, kung kailan mas ligtas sila sa mga mananakop.
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa stick insect mogawas ug mokaon panahon sa gabii, kon mas luwas sila gikan sa mga manunukob.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Still, calm water such as in a lake or a rain puddle acts like a mirror
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes reflection of light from a water surface, but the competency specifically requires guided investigations using plane and curved mirrors and refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Still, calm water such as in a lake or a rain puddle acts like a mirror
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on light behavior (reflection) but does not explore sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, or its uses in everyday situations in a way that directly supports the guided science activities described. It is a single observation, not an exploration or description of light sources or uses.

copy.en: Still, calm water such as in a lake or a rain puddle acts like a mirror — you can see the reflection of the sky, trees, or your own face in it!
copy.tl: Ang tahimik at malinaw na tubig tulad ng sa lawa o ng natipong ulan ay parang salamin — nakikita mo rito ang repleksyon ng langit, mga puno, o ng iyong mukha!
copy.bis: Ang kalmado ug linaw nga tubig sama sa lanaw o sa natipon nga ulan murag salamin — makita nimo niini ang repleksyon sa langit, mga kahoy, o sa imong nawong!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Calm, still water in a lake reflects light like a mirror
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a single example of light reflection (water acting like a mirror). G3-F-6 requires participation in guided activities to explore and describe sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, and its uses. The card does not address sources, uses, or any guided activity, and only touches on one behavior of light without instructional support for the competency's scope.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Calm, still water in a lake reflects light like a mirror
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: G8-F-11 requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection using plane and curved mirrors and refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms, with everyday applications. The card mentions reflection by water but does not involve mirrors, refraction, investigations, or illustrations. It is only a related example of reflection, not direct support for the competency.

copy.en: Calm, still water in a lake reflects light like a mirror, showing a perfect image of the sky above!
copy.tl: Ang tahimik at kalmadong tubig ng lawa ay tumatalbog ng liwanag tulad ng salamin, nagpapakita ng larawan ng langit!
copy.bis: Ang hilom ug kalmado nga tubig sa lanaw mobalik sa kahayag sama sa salamin, nagpakita sa hulagway sa langit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Stirring speeds up dissolving because it spreads the solute through the solvent much faster!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how different factors affect the solubility of a solute in a given solvent, such as heat
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses the rate of dissolving due to stirring, not the amount that dissolves (solubility) or factors such as heat that affect solubility. Stirring is a rate factor, not a solubility factor, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Stirring speeds up dissolving because it spreads the solute through the solvent much faster!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions solute and solvent but does not describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. It only explains why stirring speeds dissolving, so it does not directly support classifying or describing mixtures.

copy.en:
Why does stirring a drink make the sugar dissolve faster?

Stirring speeds up dissolving because it spreads the solute through the solvent much faster!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mabilis natutunaw ang asukal sa inumin kapag hinahalo?

Nagpapabilis ang paghahalo ng pagkatunaw dahil mas mabilis kumalat ang solute sa solvent!
copy.bis:
Nganong mas paspas matunaw ang asukal sa ilimnon kon kutawon?

Makapadali sa pagkatunaw ang pagkutaw kay mas paspas nga magkatag ang solute sa solvent!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We use a stopwatch! It's a clock that measures how long something takes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card only addresses measuring time with a stopwatch; it does not mention measuring distance, which is a required part of the competency (distance and time).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: to tell us how fast or slow it is
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that time tells how fast or slow something is, but it does not define speed as distance per time, nor does it connect distance and time. It only hints at the concept without teaching the relationship.

copy.en:
How do we know exactly how fast someone runs in a race?

We use a stopwatch! It's a clock that measures how long something takes — like counting seconds in a race — to tell us how fast or slow it is.
copy.tl:
Paano natin malalaman kung gaano kabilis tumakbo ang isang tao sa lumba?

Gumagamit tayo ng stopwatch! Ito ay orasan na sumusukat kung gaano katagal ang isang bagay — tulad ng bilang ng segundo sa takbuhan — para malaman kung gaano kabilis o kabagal.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato paghibaw kung unsa kapaspas ang pagdagan sa usa ka tawo sa lumba?

Naggamit kita og stopwatch! Kini usa ka orasan nga nagsukod kung unsa kadugay ang usa ka butang — sama sa segundos sa lumba — aron mahibal-an kung unsa kapaspas o kahinay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: when there's nothing left to eat nearby, their hidden stash keeps them going
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card focuses on the behavior of storing food as a survival strategy, not on identifying the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It implies food is needed but does not directly teach the identification of basic needs.

copy.en: Animals that store food have a secret survival trick — when there's nothing left to eat nearby, their hidden stash keeps them going.
copy.tl: May sikretong paraan ang mga hayop na nag-iimbak ng pagkain — kapag walang matira sa paligid, ang kanilang itinagong pagkain ang tumutulong sa kanilang mabuhay.
copy.bis: Adunay sekreto nga pamaagi ang mga mananap nga nagtigom og pagkaon — kon wala nay makaon sa palibot, ang ilang gitagoan nga pagkaon ang motabang nila mabuhi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Store breakable items, harmful chemicals, and flammable materials on the lowermost secured shelves so they cannot fall and cause injury or fire during shaking.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card is an earthquake safety instruction about storing breakables. It does not explore or describe factors affecting the movement of objects (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture). The mention of 'fall' and 'shaking' is incidental and not instructional about movement.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Store breakable items, harmful chemicals, and flammable materials on the lowermost secured shelves so they cannot fall and cause injury or fire during shaking.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not observe or describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object. It is a safety tip for earthquake preparedness, not a lesson on gravity. No gravitational concepts are taught.

copy.en: Store breakable items, harmful chemicals, and flammable materials on the lowermost secured shelves so they cannot fall and cause injury or fire during shaking.
copy.tl: Itago ang mga babasagin, mapanganib na kemikal, at mga materyales na madaling masunog sa pinakamababang matibay na estante para hindi mahulog at makasakit o magdulot ng sunog habang lumilindol.
copy.bis: Itago ang mga dali mabuak, peligrosong kemikal, ug mga materyales nga dali masunog sa pinakaubos nga lig-on nga estante aron dili matumba ug makasakit o makapahinabog sunog samtang maglinog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: tropical depression
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the parts and functions, and demonstrate proper handling and storing of a compound microscope
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes storm categories (tropical depression and tropical storm wind speeds). It has no relation to the compound microscope, its parts, functions, or handling/storing, which is the subject of G7-L-1.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: tropical depression
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about weather/storm categories, not about unicellular vs. multicellular organisms. It provides no support for recognizing that some organisms consist of a single cell and others of many cells.

copy.en: Before a storm becomes a typhoon, it starts as a tropical depression with winds of 35 to 64 kph, then a tropical storm with winds of 65 to 118 kph.
copy.tl: Bago maging typhoon ang isang bagyo, nagsisimula muna ito bilang tropical depression na may hanging 35 hanggang 64 kph, pagkatapos ay tropical storm na may 65 hanggang 118 kph.
copy.bis: Sa dili pa mahimong typhoon ang usa ka bagyo, magsugod kini isip tropical depression nga adunay hangin nga 35 ngadto sa 64 kph, dayon tropical storm nga adunay 65 ngadto sa 118 kph.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: So we know how strong the winds will be and when to take cover before and during a typhoon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the purpose of PAGASA storm warning signals (knowing wind strength and when to take cover) but does not describe the specific weather conditions associated with any Public Storm Warning Signal, such as wind speed ranges or expected impacts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: So we know how strong the winds will be and when to take cover before and during a typhoon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions before and during a typhoon but does not describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone. It only gives a general reason for issuing warnings, not the actual weather conditions.

copy.en:
Why does PAGASA issue storm warning signals?

So we know how strong the winds will be and when to take cover before and during a typhoon!
copy.tl:
Bakit nagbibigay ang PAGASA ng storm warning signals?

Para malaman natin kung gaano kalakas ang hangin at kung kailan dapat mag-ingat at magtago bago at habang may bagyo!
copy.bis:
Nganong naghatag ang PAGASA ug storm warning signals?

Aron mahibaw-an nato kung unsa ka kusog ang hangin ug kanus-a kinahanglan mag-amping ug magtago sa dili pa ug samtang naa pay bagyo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: heavy rain and strong winds can cause floods and landslides
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes stormy weather dangers (floods, landslides). It has no content about electromagnets, their construction, or properties.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: heavy rain and strong winds can cause floods and landslides
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about weather hazards, not magnets or magnetic properties. No instructional support for guided investigations of magnets.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: heavy rain and strong winds can cause floods and landslides
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses storm dangers, not mixture separation techniques such as decantation, filtering, or sieving. Unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Why is stormy weather dangerous?

Because heavy rain and strong winds can cause floods and landslides, which can damage homes and hurt people!
copy.tl:
Bakit mapanganib ang bagyo?

Dahil ang malakas na ulan at hangin ay maaaring magdulot ng baha at landslide, na nakakasira ng mga bahay at nakakasakit ng tao!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga delikado ang bagyo?

Tungod kay ang kusog nga ulan ug hangin makapahinabo og baha ug landslide, nga makaguba sa mga balay ug makapasakit sa mga tao!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The air there is calm and above most clouds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air and clouds, which are weather-related, but it does not teach identifying weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, or cloud cover. It only explains why flights are smooth in the stratosphere.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The air there is calm and above most clouds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air and clouds as non-living things, but it does not involve guided activities to locate and describe non-living things in and around school. The context is the stratosphere and flight comfort, not the school environment.

copy.en: Big airplanes fly in the lowest part of the stratosphere! The air there is calm and above most clouds, making the ride super smooth and less bumpy.
copy.tl: Lumilipad ang malalaking eroplano sa pinakaibaba ng stratosphere! Kalmado ang hangin at nasa ibabaw ng mga ulap doon, kaya mas maayos at hindi umaalog ang biyahe.
copy.bis: Mulupad ang dagkong eroplano sa pinakaubos nga bahin sa stratosphere! Kalmado ang hangin ug ibabaw sa mga panganod, busa mas hapsay ug dili kaayo muuyog ang biyahe.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We breathe O2 with two oxygen atoms.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses O2 and O3, not air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It does not describe the composition of air or mention the other gases, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ozone is O3, with three!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions O2 and O3 as chemical species but does not describe pure substances having fixed chemical composition, elements vs compounds, or the unique number of protons in atoms. It only touches on molecular formulas, which is not the focus of this competency.

copy.en: We breathe O2 with two oxygen atoms. Ozone is O3, with three! It blocks UV rays up high, but it’s toxic if we breathe it.
copy.tl: Ang hinihinga natin ay O2, na may dalawang oxygen atoms. Ang ozone naman ay O3, may tatlong atoms! Magaling itong manalag sa UV sa itaas, pero nakakalason kung hihingahin.
copy.bis: Ang atong ginhawa mao ang O2, nga adunay duha ka oxygen atoms. Ang ozone mao ang O3, adunay tulo ka atoms! Maayo kini mosalipod sa UV sa taas, apan makahilo kon ginhawaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: hot flows and rocks often race down the exact same valleys used in past eruptions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes where volcanic flows travel on steep stratovolcanoes, but does not address discussing eruption patterns over the last 100 years, family/community discussion, or assessing predictability. It shares the broad topic of volcanic activity but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Where do hot flows and rocks go on steep stratovolcanoes?

Many Philippine volcanoes are steep stratovolcanoes! Because of this, hot flows and rocks often race down the exact same valleys used in past eruptions.
copy.tl:
Saan pumupunta ang mainit na lava at bato sa mga matarik na bulkan?

Maraming bulkan sa Pilipinas ay matarik na stratovolcano! Kaya madalas, ang mainit na lava at bato ay nagmamadali pababa sa parehong lambak na ginamit noon.
copy.bis:
Asa mopadulong ang init nga lava ug bato sa mga matarik nga bulkan?

Daghan nga bulkan sa Pilipinas kay matarik nga stratovolcano! Mao nga ang init nga lava ug bato kanunay nagdagan paubos sa parehas nga mga walog nga gigamit sa miaging pagputok.

copy.tl: Kuskusin ang mineral sa magaspang na tile! Ang pulbos na naiiwan, o streak, ay minsan iba sa kulay ng bato, at nakakatulong itong makilala ang mineral!
copy.bis: Gaskason ang mineral sa gaspang nga tisa! Ang pulbos nga mabilin, o streak, usahay lahi sa kolor sa bato, ug makatabang kini aron mailhan ang mineral!

copy.en: An acid's strength is different from its concentration! Strength is how readily it releases H+, while concentration is how much acid is in the water.
copy.tl: Ang lakas ng acid ay iba sa konsentrasyon! Ang lakas ay kung gaano kadaling maglabas ng H+, habang ang konsentrasyon ay kung gaano karami ang acid sa tubig.
copy.bis: Ang kakusog sa acid lahi sa konsentrasyon! Ang kakusog mao kung unsa kadali magpagawas og H+, samtang ang konsentrasyon mao kung pila ka daghan ang acid sa tubig.

copy.tl: Ang pag-unat o stretching ay nagpapalambot sa ating mga kalamnan at kasukasuan, kaya mas madali tayong gumalaw.
copy.bis: Ang pag-inat makapahumok sa atong mga unod ug lutahan, mao nga mas sayon ta molihok.

copy.en:
What is the difference between strong and weak acids?

A strong acid like muriatic acid releases almost all its H+ in water! A weak acid like vinegar releases only a small part.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng strong at weak acid?

Ang strong acid tulad ng muriatic acid ay halos buong naglalabas ng H+ sa tubig! Ang weak acid tulad ng suka ay bahagya lang.
copy.bis:
Unsay kalahian sa strong ug weak acid?

Ang strong acid sama sa muriatic acid hapit tanan nga H+ niini gipagawas sa tubig! Ang weak acid sama sa suka gamay ra.

copy.en: A stronger magnet can pull out way more iron than a weak magnet can!
copy.tl: Mas maraming bakal ang kayang hanguin ng malakas na magneto kaysa sa mahinang magneto!
copy.bis: Mas daghang puthaw ang makuha sa kusgan nga magneto kaysa sa luya nga magneto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Concrete is super strong when squeezed (compression) but weak when pulled (tension). Steel is strong in both!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Concrete is super strong when squeezed (compression) but weak when pulled (tension). Steel is strong in both!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions squeezing (compression) and pulling (tension), which are forces that can change shape, but it does not determine how forces change the shape of objects. The competency requires determining how forces change shape, which is not directly supported.

copy.en:
Why do builders mix concrete and steel together?

Concrete is super strong when squeezed (compression) but weak when pulled (tension). Steel is strong in both! Together they make reinforced concrete.
copy.tl:
Bakit pinaghahalo ng mga builder ang semento at bakal?

Ang semento ay malakas kapag pinipiga (compression) pero mahina kapag hinahila (tension). Malakas ang bakal sa dalawa! Kaya pinagsasama sila.
copy.bis:
Nganong gisagol sa mga builder ang semento ug bakal?

Ang semento lig-on kung pinislak (compression) pero mahuyang kung bawion (tension). Ang bakal lig-on sa duha! Mao nga gihiusa sila.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains diagonal bracing as a structural technique to prevent buildings from racking. It does not demonstrate that pushes and pulls change the speed or direction of an object, nor does it involve activities about making objects go faster, turn, slow down, or stop. The mention of wind or earthquakes pushing is about external forces on a building, not about changing an object's motion as required by the competency.

copy.en:
Ever notice X-shaped braces on buildings?

That's diagonal bracing! It adds triangles inside the frame, stopping it from leaning sideways when wind or earthquakes push.
copy.tl:
Napansin mo ba ang mga X-shaped na brace sa mga gusali?

Iyan ang diagonal bracing! Nagdadagdag ito ng triangles sa loob ng frame, pinipigilan itong kumiling kapag hinahangin o nililindol.
copy.bis:
Nakita ba nimo ang mga X-shaped nga brace sa mga building?

Mao na ang diagonal bracing! Nagdugang kini og triangles sa sulod sa frame, nagpugong niini sa pagliko kung hangin o lindol.

Why do scientists study plants and animals in their habitats?

By watching organisms where they naturally live, scientists learn how ecosystems work and how to protect them through conservation, which means keeping nature safe.
copy.tl:
Bakit pinag-aaralan ng mga scientist ang mga halaman at hayop sa kanilang mga habitat?

Sa pamamagitan ng pagmamasid sa mga organismo kung saan sila natural na naninirahan, natututuhan ng mga scientist kung paano gumagana ang mga ecosystem at kung paano ito mapoprotektahan sa pamamagitan ng conservation, ibig sabihin pag-iingat sa kalikasan.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga gitun-an sa mga scientist ang mga tanom ug mananap sa ilang mga habitat?

Pinaagi sa pag-obserbar sa mga organismo diin sila natural nga nagpuyo, makat-on ang mga scientist kon giunsa paglihok ang mga ecosystem ug kon unsaon kini pagpanalipod pinaagi sa conservation, nga nagpasabot pag-amping sa kinaiyahan.

copy.en: Many ice boxes are made of styrofoam! It is full of tiny air pockets that help slow down heat.
copy.tl: Maraming ice box ang gawa sa styrofoam! Puno ito ng maliliit na bula ng hangin na nagpapabagal sa init.
copy.bis: Daghang ice box ang hinimo sa styrofoam! Puno kini sa gagmay nga bula sa hangin nga magpahinay sa kainit.

Why can sweet drinks be bad for us?

Sweet drinks like soda and juice hold large amounts of hidden, dissolved sugar. Drinking them often can harm our teeth and health!
copy.tl:
Bakit nakasasama ang mga matamis na inumin?

Ang mga matamis na inumin tulad ng softdrinks at juice ay may malaking dami ng natunaw na asukal. Ang madalas na pag-inom nito ay makasama sa ngipin at kalusugan!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga makadaot ang tam-is nga ilimnon?

Ang tam-is nga ilimnon sama sa softdrinks ug juice adunay daghang natunaw nga asukal. Ang kanunay nga pag-inom niini makadaot sa ngipon ug panglawas!

How does lots of sugar make jam last longer?

The sugar pulls water out of the microbes, helping the food last much longer!
copy.tl:
Paano pinapatagal ng napakaraming asukal ang jam?

Hinahagop ng asukal ang tubig palabas ng mikrobyo, kaya tumatagal ang pagkain!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpadugay sa daghang asukal sa jam?

Gisuyop sa asukal ang tubig gikan sa mikrobyo, busa modugay ang pagkaon!

copy.bis: Ang bagasse mao ang nahibilin nga tangkay sa tubo human makuha ang duga — mahimong sunugon kini isip biofuel para sa kuryente, o gamiton sa paghimo og papel ug cardboard!

copy.en:
What sugar is inside sugarcane?

The sweet juice in sugarcane is sucrose — the very same white sugar we use at home!
copy.tl:
Anong asukal ang nasa loob ng tubo?

Ang matamis na katas ng tubo ay sucrose (sukrosa) — ito rin ang puting asukal na ginagamit natin sa bahay!
copy.bis:
Unsang asukal ang naa sa sulod sa tubo?

Ang tam-is nga duga sa tubo mao ang sucrose (sukrosa) — mao ra usab kini ang puti nga asukal nga atong gigamit sa balay!

copy.en: Sunlight takes just 8 minutes to reach Earth from the Sun's surface. But photons born in the Sun's core do a bumpy 'random walk' — bouncing around for 1 to 10 million years before finally escaping!
copy.tl: Ang ilaw mula sa surface ng Araw ay umaabot sa Earth sa loob ng 8 minuto. Pero ang mga photon sa core ng Araw ay gumagawa ng 'random walk' — tumatalon-talon ng 1 hanggang 10 milyong taon bago makalabas!
copy.bis: Ang suga gikan sa nawong sa Adlaw makaabut sa Yuta sulod sa 8 minuto. Apan ang mga photon sa core sa Adlaw naghimo og 'random walk' — nagtambay-tambay sulod sa 1 hangtod 10 ka milyon ka tuig sa wala pa makagawas!

copy.tl: Kapag naubos na ng Araw ang hydrogen nito, lalobo ito at magiging isang malaking pulang bituin na tinatawag na red giant!
copy.bis: Kung mahurot na sa Adlaw ang hydrogen niini, mohabok kini ug mahimong dako nga pula nga bituon nga gitawag red giant!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun! When solar wind particles hit the air high above Earth near the poles

copy.en:
What causes the beautiful, colorful auroras in the sky?

The Sun! When solar wind particles hit the air high above Earth near the poles, the air glows and turns into colorful lights.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagdudulot ng makukulay na aurora sa langit?

Ang Araw! Kapag tumama ang mga particle mula sa solar wind sa hangin sa itaas ng Mundo malapit sa mga poste, nagliliwanag ito at nagiging makukulay na ilaw.
copy.bis:
Unsay hinungdan sa bulokon nga aurora sa langit?

Ang Adlaw! Kung ang mga particle gikan sa solar wind moigo sa hangin sa taas sa Kalibutan duol sa mga poste, modan-ag kini ug mahimong bulokon nga kahayag.
